description: The hot mutex of the state store: a link-created record file for the fast path, and a kernel lock (the registry row of the same name) that serialises the cleanup of a dead holder's record. Node implements it in src/state/hot-lock.mjs until the state store moves to Rust.

state.note: <fgosDir> is the .fgos of the checkout that owns the log

record.platforms: without /proc the record is {v, pid, bootId?}: the judge then answers unknown for a live pid and the record is never cleaned (fail closed)
record.creation: written whole to a temp file in the same directory, then link()ed onto the record path; the record path never exists half-written

allOf: the judge of the recorded tuple answers dead (zombie counts as dead; alive and unknown never qualify)
the cleaner holds the kernel lock <resource>.reclaim
the record is read again under that kernel lock and its bytes equal the bytes the judge saw
only then unlink the record, release the kernel lock, and try the link again
never: a record that does not parse is never cleaned
a record whose judge answers unknown is never cleaned (an observer outside the initial pid namespace judging a record without pidNs is unknown)

criticalSection.callback: synchronous; a thenable result is an error
criticalSection.writes: every write goes through the transaction object, which is revoked when the callback returns
forbidden: starting a child process (any child_process export, including named ESM imports)
acquiring a hot mutex again in the same process

exec-under-hot-lock.meaning: a child process was started inside the critical section; thrown at the call, with the stack

hot-lock-reentry.meaning: a hot mutex was acquired while this process already holds one; thrown at once, without waiting

hot-lock-timeout.meaning: the record stayed held (or unjudgeable) for the whole wait; carries holder pid and, when the record could not be read, reason lock-record-unreadable

lock-record-unreadable.meaning: reason on hot-lock-timeout: the record exists but does not parse; only an owner running `fgos lock fence` clears it

state-tx-revoked.meaning: a transaction object was used after its callback returned

state-tx-async.meaning: the callback returned a thenable; the lock is already released when this is thrown
